statement: Operad: objects Ob(O); for each object y, finite n and family x, a set O_n(x;y); identities id_x in O_1(x;x); composition with laws phi o (id,...,id)=phi, id_y o phi = phi, and associativity (Def 2.1.2)
work: Spivak 2013, arXiv:1305.0297 (preprint, no DOI)
note: Operad law 'a wiring diagram of wiring diagrams is a wiring diagram'. Cluster letter guessed; no research map in context.

statement: Main operad S: objects finite sets; a morphism X_1,...,X_n -> Y is a cospan X_1 ⊔...⊔ X_n -> C <- Y up to isomorphism of C; composition by pushout of the middle square (Example 2.1.7)
work: Spivak 2013, arXiv:1305.0297 (preprint, no DOI)
note: Operands are finite sets of wires (stars); semantics shown is relations, which carry no time.

statement: Algebra on an operad is an operad functor O -> Sets; Rel_A(X) = P(A^X); phi-conjunction: pullback Q of R_1x...xR_n -> A^{X_1⊔...⊔X_n} <- A^C, then image of Q in A^Y (Def 2.2.1, Example 2.2.10)
work: Spivak 2013, arXiv:1305.0297 (preprint, no DOI)

statement: Rel_A respects the composition formula (7) of S, because epi-mono factorisations in Set are unique (Example 2.2.10)
work: Spivak 2013, arXiv:1305.0297 (preprint, no DOI)

statement: Conjecture 3.1.6: Rel_A is quotient-free (any epimorphism of algebras out of Rel_A is an isomorphism or lands on the terminal algebra)
work: Spivak 2013, arXiv:1305.0297 (preprint, no DOI)
note: A conjecture, not a theorem. Section 3 was skimmed only by heading per the file's read list, so the provenance is set to sa. The file's reading that this says no simplifying summary survives wiring is its own gloss.

statement: Lemma 4.1.2 extends Rel_A to a single algebra Rel on the typed operad T; Proposition 4.3.1 lifts Rel to join-semilattices for disjunctive queries
work: Spivak 2013, arXiv:1305.0297 (preprint, no DOI)
note: Sections 3 to 5 skimmed by heading only. Validation corrected the credit: the extension to T is Lemma 4.1.2, not Proposition 4.3.1.

statement: Open dynamical system (Def 2.9): smooth manifolds M (state), U^in, U^out; maps f^in: M x U^in -> TM with f^in(m,u) in T_m M, and f^out: M -> U^out; the readout depends on the state alone, not on the input
work: Vagner, Spivak, Lerman 2015, TAC 30 (2015) 1793-1822, DOI 10.70930/tac/7tz1nkbd; arXiv:1408.1598v2
note: Linear case: Euclidean spaces and linear f.

statement: Feedback as substitution (Remark 2.12): F'(m,a) = F(m,a,g_B(m)); two-system version F'(m_1,m_2,a) = (F_1(m_1,a,g_B(m_2)), F_2(m_2,g_1(m_1)))
work: Vagner, Spivak, Lerman 2015, TAC 30 (2015) 1793-1822, DOI 10.70930/tac/7tz1nkbd; arXiv:1408.1598v2

statement: Box X = (X^in, X^out) of typed finite sets; wiring diagram Phi: X -> Y is (X, Y, phi) with phi a typed bijection X^in + Y^out -> X^out + Y^in and no passing wires, phi(Y^out) ∩ Y^in = empty (Def 3.1; rationale Remark 3.7)
work: Vagner, Spivak, Lerman 2015, TAC 30 (2015) 1793-1822, DOI 10.70930/tac/7tz1nkbd; arXiv:1408.1598v2
note: Bijection: every inner input fed by exactly one source, no port dangling, nothing split. Relevant to file's own worked example, which violated it (see worked-example line).

statement: (W, ⊕, 0) is a symmetric monoidal category, with monoidal product X_1 ⊕ X_2 = (X_1^in + X_2^in, X_1^out + X_2^out) and unit 0 = (∅,∅) (Def 3.8, Prop 3.11)
work: Vagner, Spivak, Lerman 2015, TAC 30 (2015) 1793-1822, DOI 10.70930/tac/7tz1nkbd; arXiv:1408.1598v2
note: Structural result only.

statement: Algebra G (Def 4.2): for Phi = (X,Y,phi), G(Phi)(S,f) = (S,g) with the state space unchanged, g^out = phi^out ∘ f^out, and g^in(s,y) = f^in(s, phi^in(f^out(s), y)); coherence mu((S,f),(S',f')) = (S+S', f x f')
work: Vagner, Spivak, Lerman 2015, TAC 30 (2015) 1793-1822, DOI 10.70930/tac/7tz1nkbd; arXiv:1408.1598v2
note: Read out members, route through wiring, feed routed signals to input slots, expose a subset of readouts.

statement: Proposition 4.5: (G, mu) is a lax monoidal functor, i.e. a W-algebra
work: Vagner, Spivak, Lerman 2015, TAC 30 (2015) 1793-1822, DOI 10.70930/tac/7tz1nkbd; arXiv:1408.1598v2
note: The functoriality theorem the file calls the only proved composition law for dynamics. Proves no dynamical property.

statement: Algebra L (Def 5.4), linear systems in blocks f = [[f^{S,S}, f^{S,X}],[f^{X,S}, 0]]: the wired system has g^{S,S} = f^{S,X} phi^{X,X} f^{X,S} + f^{S,S}
work: Vagner, Spivak, Lerman 2015, TAC 30 (2015) 1793-1822, DOI 10.70930/tac/7tz1nkbd; arXiv:1408.1598v2
note: f^{S,X} is how inputs push the state, f^{X,S} the readout, phi^{X,X} the inner routing.

statement: Proposition 5.5: L is a W_Lin-algebra
work: Vagner, Spivak, Lerman 2015, TAC 30 (2015) 1793-1822, DOI 10.70930/tac/7tz1nkbd; arXiv:1408.1598v2
Vagner, Spivak, Lerman 2015, TAC 30 (2015) 1793-1822, DOI 10.70930/tac/7tz1nkbd; arXiv:1408.1598v2
note: Textbook salt-tank worked exercise (Boyce and DiPrima), not a data fit. Each box knows only its own inputs and outputs.

statement: VSL states no dynamical-property theorem: Propositions 3.11, 4.5 and 5.5 are structural only, and a text search for stability, equilibrium, Lipschitz and existence finds nothing
work: Vagner, Spivak, Lerman 2015, TAC 30 (2015) 1793-1822, DOI 10.70930/tac/7tz1nkbd; arXiv:1408.1598v2
note: Negative claim, recorded as equation because the schema has no kind for an absent theorem. Search-based, so it reports absence in the read text only.

statement: Deterministic system (Def 1.2.1.2): a lens (update_S, expose_S): (State, State) <-> (In, Out) with expose: State -> Out and update: State x In -> State; the pair (Out, In) is the interface
work: Myers, Categorical Systems Theory, draft 2023-09-03 (davidjaz.com/Papers/DynamicalBook.pdf; no DOI)
note: Draft self-described as 'work in progress ... Use at your own peril!'. Chapters 3 to 6 not read.

statement: Differential system (Def 1.2.2.1): ds_k/dt = update_S^k(s, i) over R^n with m parameters and k exposed variables
work: Myers, Categorical Systems Theory, draft 2023-09-03 (davidjaz.com/Papers/DynamicalBook.pdf; no DOI)

statement: Lens (Def 1.3.1.1) f = (f, f#): (A-, A+) <-> (B-, B+): passforward f: A+ -> B+ and passback f#: A+ x B- -> A-
work: Myers, Categorical Systems Theory, draft 2023-09-03 (davidjaz.com/Papers/DynamicalBook.pdf; no DOI)
note: The passback lets a wiring carry a signal in the reverse direction.

statement: Lens composite (Def 1.3.1.2): passforward g∘f; passback (a+, c-) -> f#(a+, g#(f(a+), c-))
work: Myers, Categorical Systems Theory, draft 2023-09-03 (davidjaz.com/Papers/DynamicalBook.pdf; no DOI)

statement: Composing a system with a lens w gives a system with the same states: update'(s, i') = update_S(s, w#(expose_S(s), i')) and expose'(s) = w(expose_S(s))
work: Myers, Categorical Systems Theory, draft 2023-09-03 (davidjaz.com/Papers/DynamicalBook.pdf; no DOI)
note: The file's own unfolding of Defs 1.2.1.2 and 1.3.1.2; same formula as VSL Def 4.2. Parallel product: update((s1,s2),(i1,i2)) = (update_1, update_2).

statement: City in a multi-city SIR model (Def 1.3.2.8): differential system with state (S,I,R), input in R^3 x R^3, exposing the whole state; third component of update printed as k_1 I
work: Myers, Categorical Systems Theory, draft 2023-09-03 (davidjaz.com/Papers/DynamicalBook.pdf; no DOI)
note: The printed k_1 I is almost certainly a typo for k_2 I (recovery must balance -k_2 I). Validation confirmed the source prints k_1 I.

statement: Fear as a state a person can have: seeing a scary snake makes me recoil and feel fear, seeing a cute plushie makes me go over and pet it
work: Myers, Categorical Systems Theory, draft 2023-09-03 (davidjaz.com/Papers/DynamicalBook.pdf; no DOI)
note: Motivation sentence in chapter 1, not a model. The file says so.

statement: Person as relational agency (Spivak 2013 section 1): a person maintains a relationship between what she sees, hears, feels and does, representable as a 4-ary relation; the same hierarchical structures extend to interactions between multiple humans and machines
work: Spivak 2013, arXiv:1305.0297 (preprint, no DOI)
note: A motivating remark; the file says no development toward people follows.

statement: F-decorated cospan (Def 3.1): given C with finite colimits and lax monoidal (F, phi): (C,+) -> (D,⊗), a cospan X -> N <- Y with decoration s: 1 -> F N; morphisms are maps of cospans n with F n ∘ s = s'
work: Fong 2015, Decorated cospans, TAC 30(33) (2015) 1096-1120, DOI 10.70930/tac/8cw8rvm2; arXiv:1502.00872v3

statement: Proposition 3.2: FCospan composition is the pushout N +_Y M with composite decoration 1 -> 1⊗1 -> F N⊗F M -> F(N+M) -> F(N +_Y M)
work: Fong 2015, Decorated cospans, TAC 30(33) (2015) 1096-1120, DOI 10.70930/tac/8cw8rvm2; arXiv:1502.00872v3
note: Remark 3.3: the copair encodes identification of the overlap, merging the two decorations.

statement: Theorem 3.4: if F is lax braided monoidal into a braided monoidal (D,⊗), FCospan is symmetric monoidal and a hypergraph category, with a wide embedding Cospan(C) into FCospan
work: Fong 2015, Decorated cospans, TAC 30(33) (2015) 1096-1120, DOI 10.70930/tac/8cw8rvm2; arXiv:1502.00872v3

statement: Resistor network (Fong section 5): power function Q(psi) = Σ_e (1/r(e)) (psi_t(e) - psi_s(e))^2; semantics the linear subspace {(phi, ∇Q phi) : phi in R^N}
work: Fong 2015, Decorated cospans, TAC 30(33) (2015) 1096-1120, DOI 10.70930/tac/8cw8rvm2; arXiv:1502.00872v3
note: Circuit example; section 5 read, section 4 and appendix not read.

statement: Decorated cospans as used in Fong 2015 for labelled-graph decorations: applications 'were flawed'
work: Fong 2015, TAC 30(33) DOI 10.70930/tac/8cw8rvm2 vs Baez, Courser, Vasilakopoulou 2022, Compositionality 4 (2022) 3, DOI 10.32408/compositionality-4-3
note: Side A: Fong 2015 functor into Set decorates with graphs. Side B: BCV say a functor into Set cannot decorate the apex with a graph (two graphs on the same nodes are distinct decorations, blocking lax monoidality); repair needs pseudofunctors into Cat and a double category. Verdict per file: the BCV correction is taken; anything using Fong 2015 for labelled-graph or Petri-net decorations is read through it.

statement: Baez-Fong Theorem 1.1: a hypergraph functor □: Circ -> LagRel, mapping finite X to F^X ⊕ (F^X)* and an open circuit to the Lagrangian relation ⋃_{v in Graph(dQ)} S_{t i(v)} x S_{o(v)}, Q the circuit's power functional
note: Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 7.7 as stated; file's ASCII transcription of the notation. Proofs not read.

statement: Principle of minimum power, corrected form: total power dissipated = 2P(phi), with P(phi) = (1/2) Σ_e (1/r(e)) (phi(t(e)) - phi(s(e)))^2; with boundary potentials fixed, interior potentials minimise it, giving a boundary Dirichlet form Q (the power functional)
note: Validation corrected a misplaced factor of two in the introduction's formula; this is the corrected form. The authors' restriction: 'We only study circuits built from passive components: that is, those that do not produce energy.'

statement: Reaction-network rate equation (Def 13): dc/dt = Σ_tau r(tau)(t(tau) - s(tau)) c^{s(tau)}, with c^{s(tau)} = ∏_sigma c_sigma^{s(tau)(sigma)}
note: Chemistry; SIRS epidemic model is the first example. No drives.

statement: Open dynamical system from X to Y (Def 14): a cospan X -> S <- Y with an algebraic vector field v on R^S; open rate equation dc/dt = v(c) + i_*(I) - o_*(O), with i_*(I)_sigma = Σ_{x: i(x)=sigma} I_x

Lemmas 15 and 16: D(f)(v) = f_* ∘ v ∘ f^* (pullback copies, pushforward sums over fibres); D is lax symmetric monoidal with delta(v,v') = i_* ∘ v ∘ i^* + i'_* ∘ v' ∘ i'^* (add vector fields on a disjoint union)
note: Summing law: contributions to a shared variable add. The file's candidate law for pooled quantities such as morale.

statement: Theorem 17: composite of open dynamical systems is the cospan S +_Y S' with vector field D([j,j']) ∘ delta applied to (v, v'); Dynam is a hypergraph category
Theorem 18: gray-boxing RxNet -> Dynam (open reaction network to its vector field) is a symmetric monoidal functor

Theorem 23: black-boxing Dynam -> SemiAlgRel is a symmetric monoidal functor sending an open dynamical system to the relation between inputs, outputs, inflows and outflows it imposes in steady state; composition of semialgebraic relations via Tarski-Seidenberg
note: The only property-level composition law in the file, and it concerns steady states, not stability or oscillation. Authors say multiple steady states are possible and their proof 'sidesteps this issue'.

statement: One-coloured network model (Def 2): a lax symmetric monoidal functor F: S -> Mon; Theorem 3 unpacks it to sets F(n), an overlay ∪, permutations, a disjoint union ⊔, and twelve equations
work: Baez, Foley, Moeller, Pollard 2020, TAC 35 (2020) 700-744, DOI 10.70930/tac/e0rrdvk5; arXiv:1711.00037v4
note: Static: no dynamics, no states. General definition is F: S(C) -> Cat (file's cross-check); Def 2 is the one-coloured Mon case.

statement: Theorem 49: the network operad has operations O_F(n_1,...,n_k; n) = S_n x F(n) if n_1+...+n_k = n, empty otherwise
work: Baez, Foley, Moeller, Pollard 2020, TAC 35 (2020) 700-744, DOI 10.70930/tac/e0rrdvk5; arXiv:1711.00037v4

statement: Example 53 (canonical algebra): alpha(sigma, g)(h_1,...,h_k) = g ∪ sigma(h_1 ⊔ ... ⊔ h_k): place sub-networks side by side, relabel vertices, then overlay the group's own extra edges g
work: Baez, Foley, Moeller, Pollard 2020, TAC 35 (2020) 700-744, DOI 10.70930/tac/e0rrdvk5; arXiv:1711.00037v4
note: Formal version of 'a group is its members plus the ties among them'. Candidate 'who is tied to whom' layer; not combined with dynamics in any source read.

statement: Structured cospan: for a functor L: A -> X with finite colimits and L a left adjoint, a structured cospan is a diagram L(a) -> x <- L(b) in X; this gives a symmetric monoidal double category with structured cospans as horizontal 1-cells
note: Abstract and introduction read only.

statement: BCV Theorem 3.1: for A, X with finite colimits and L preserving them, a symmetric monoidal double category L Csp(X) exists, with objects of A, vertical morphisms of A, horizontal 1-cells L-structured cospans
work: Baez, Courser, Vasilakopoulou 2022, Compositionality 4 (2022) 3, DOI 10.32408/compositionality-4-3; arXiv:2101.09363v4
note: Statement read; proof not in the file's read list for this theorem.

statement: BCV Theorem 4.1: under a condition on F, the decorated-cospan double category FCsp for a symmetric lax monoidal pseudofunctor F: (A,+) -> (Cat,x) is isomorphic to L Csp(∫F), with L a left adjoint to the Grothendieck opfibration
work: Baez, Courser, Vasilakopoulou 2022, Compositionality 4 (2022) 3, DOI 10.32408/compositionality-4-3; arXiv:2101.09363v4

statement: BCV section 6.4: for open dynamical systems (F = D, vector fields on R^S) the opfibration ∫D -> FinSet has no left adjoint, so Theorem 4.1 cannot apply and decorated cospans are needed for dynamics
work: Baez, Courser, Vasilakopoulou 2022, Compositionality 4 (2022) 3, DOI 10.32408/compositionality-4-3; arXiv:2101.09363v4
note: BCV's own words: 'in some cases decorated cospans appear to be necessary'.

statement: Open game (Def 3): G: (X,S) -> (Y,R) is a 4-tuple (Sigma_G, P_G, C_G, B_G): strategy profiles, play P_G: Sigma x X -> Y, coplay C_G: Sigma x X x R -> S, best-response B_G: X x (Y -> R) -> Rel(Sigma); no conditions imposed
work: Ghani, Hedges, Winschel, Zahn 2018, LICS '18 pp. 472-481, DOI 10.1145/3209108.3209165; arXiv:1603.04641v3
note: S is coutility: values returned to the calling environment, which become utility for other processes. Preferences are fixed utilities.

statement: Composite H∘G (Def 9): Sigma = Sigma_G x Sigma_H; P((sigma,tau),x) = P_H(tau, P_G(sigma,x)); C((sigma,tau),x,q) = C_G(sigma, x, C_H(tau, P_G(sigma,x), q)); best response composes via k'(y) = C_H(tau, y, k(P_H(tau,y)))
work: Ghani, Hedges, Winschel, Zahn 2018, LICS '18 pp. 472-481, DOI 10.1145/3209108.3209165; arXiv:1603.04641v3
note: Coplay composition is composition of lenses, per the authors.

statement: Theorem 1: the category of open games is monoidal, moreover symmetric, with (X_1,S_1) ⊗ (X_2,S_2) = (X_1 x X_2, S_1 x S_2); associativity holds only up to equivalence of strategy profiles
work: Ghani, Hedges, Winschel, Zahn 2018, LICS '18 pp. 472-481, DOI 10.1145/3209108.3209165; arXiv:1603.04641v3
note: Proposition 3 (the quotient to a category) is stated in the body but not in the file's read list. Theorem 2 not read.

statement: Limits the authors state for open games: only simultaneous and sequential games, pure strategies, and the Nash solution concept built into the definition; they call for mixed strategies and subgame-perfect equilibrium
work: Ghani, Hedges, Winschel, Zahn 2018, LICS '18 pp. 472-481, DOI 10.1145/3209108.3209165; arXiv:1603.04641v3
note: Their own conclusions, not the file's gloss.

statement: No-feedthrough rule: every drive must have a state, because readout is a function of state alone, so a reflex such as startle needs a fast state variable and cannot be a direct input-to-output map
work: Vagner, Spivak, Lerman 2015, TAC 30 (2015) 1793-1822, DOI 10.70930/tac/7tz1nkbd; arXiv:1408.1598v2
note: Derived from read Definition 2.9, but the modelling stance is the file's own, flagged as judgement, and is a modelling choice rather than a fact about people.

statement: Fear and desire of a person: state (F, D); fear decays at rate a, is raised by the other's displayed fear (gain c) and by threat s; desire decays at b, is suppressed by own fear at strength m, and raised by reward w
work: none (the file's own placeholder module; parameters a, b, c, m are placeholders)
note: Own illustrative construction, not drawn from a source. Built on read VSL Def 2.9 and 5.4.

statement: Linear person module: dF/dt = -aF + c u + s; dD/dt = -bD - mF + w, with block form f^{S,S} = [[-a,0],[-m,-b]], f^{S,X} = [[c,1,0],[0,0,1]], f^{X,S} = [1,0]
work: none (the file's own placeholder module)
note: Own construction, not from a source.

statement: Group of two (VSL-conformant two-output-port version), composite matrix in (F_A, D_A, F_B, D_B): rows [-a,0,c,0], [-m,-b,0,0], [c,0,-a,0], [0,0,-m,-b]; obtained as g^{S,S} = f^{S,X} phi^{X,X} f^{X,S} + f^{S,S}
work: Vagner, Spivak, Lerman 2015, TAC 30 (2015) 1793-1822, DOI 10.70930/tac/7tz1nkbd; arXiv:1408.1598v2
note: Derived from read Def 5.4 with the module above. The file's first sketch split outputs and was not a bijection, so the conformant version is the one that counts. Symbolic equality checked by the file's computer algebra; numerics re-run in validation.

statement: Eigenvalues of the two-person composite are -a + c, -a - c, and -b (twice); the group is stable iff |c| < a (with b > 0)
work: Vagner, Spivak, Lerman 2015, TAC 30 (2015) 1793-1822, DOI 10.70930/tac/7tz1nkbd; arXiv:1408.1598v2
size_dependence: Stability condition mixes a member parameter (a) with a coupling parameter (c); the file says it is not a function of the interface alone.
note: Validation corrected the condition to |c| < a. Own computation on read definitions.

statement: Non-reciprocal wiring (gains c_A from B to A, c_B from A to B): fear block [[-a, c_A],[c_B, -a]] with eigenvalues -a ± sqrt(c_A c_B); for c_A c_B < 0 the group oscillates though each person alone decays monotonically
work: Vagner, Spivak, Lerman 2015, TAC 30 (2015) 1793-1822, DOI 10.70930/tac/7tz1nkbd; arXiv:1408.1598v2
size_dependence: Two members only; the file does not claim a general group-size result.
note: Symbolic check by the file. A symmetric (reciprocal) network of the Baez-Fong form cannot produce this.

statement: Small-gain: open-loop DC gain from u to y of one module is c/a; two modules wired back to back give loop gain (c/a)^2, which is less than 1 exactly when |c| < a
work: standard control-theory account (not read in any source per the file); cross-check cites Jiang, Teel, Praly 1994, DOI 10.1007/bf01211469 via file 044
note: File says D027 should check it against Sontag or Jiang-Teel-Praly; the cross-check discharges it only at standard-account level.

statement: Nested wiring test: a four-person group built from two pairs equals the flat four-person wiring (operad associativity); on 1,000 random states and inputs, for a nonlinear variant dF/dt = -aF + c tanh(u) + s, dD/dt = -bD - mF^2 + w, the maximum difference was 0
work: Vagner, Spivak, Lerman 2015, TAC 30 (2015) 1793-1822, DOI 10.70930/tac/7tz1nkbd; arXiv:1408.1598v2
note: Implementation check of the substitution formula, not an empirical result, and not a case of Proposition 4.5 as stated (the nested tie merges wires, outside VSL bijection). Own numerics.

statement: A drive module is a machine with an equilibrium (a set-point) and a storage function (distance from set-point).
work: none cited in 044 for this translation; file-level reading
note: A translation by 044 of its own, not a claim taken from a source. Stated as the operand for the Capucci-Myers certificate.

statement: The Keramati-Gutkin homeostatic drive function is the natural storage-function instance for a drive module.
work: Keramati & Gutkin, eLife (as read in file 016 §13; DOI not given in 044)
note: 044 calls it 'the natural instance' and does not read the source itself. The cross-check says file 016 reads the eLife paper in full and that its homeostatic distance is the storage-function candidate, so the claim is consistent with a read source but is not read in 044.

statement: Assume-guarantee for a Moore machine, eq (1.1): (u,v) |= (phi,alpha) <-> (phi,gamma) means phi(s) and alpha(i) => phi(u(s,i)), and phi(s) => gamma(v(s)).
work: Capucci, M., Myers, D. J. (2026). Compositionality of Lyapunov functions via assume-guarantee reasoning. arXiv:2604.03017 [cs.LO]; no DOI (preprint)
note: Validated against the paper in the 2026-10-29 validation log.

statement: Proof rule COMP: if a wiring diagram w is certified (outer assumption implies each inner assumption, and inner guarantees imply the outer guarantee), then w composed with (m1 || ... || mn) satisfies the outer certificate.
work: Capucci & Myers (2026), arXiv:2604.03017; no DOI (preprint)
note: Soundness is by lens composition in the category of subsets. Applies to any certified lens, including feedback, but no loop case is worked in the paper.

statement: Proof rule SUBST: if machine S' is certified and S' simulates (coarse-grains) S via sigma, then S is certified.
work: Capucci & Myers (2026), arXiv:2604.03017; no DOI (preprint)
note: Fibrancy of the certified over the uncertified machines, per the paper.

statement: Certified loose map, eq (4.7): alpha2(w(o1), a2) + kappa(gamma1(o1)) >= alpha1(w#(o1,a2)) and gamma1(o1) >= gamma2(w(o1)), with kappa in K-infinity-or-zero called the slack; certified lenses compose by lens composition and addition of slacks.
work: Capucci & Myers (2026), arXiv:2604.03017; no DOI (preprint)
note: The slack kappa is the quantity a loop would need to satisfy a gain condition, per 044 section 6 item 1 (not shown in the paper).

statement: Eq (4.9)-(4.10): an equilibrium of an open ODE is LISS iff it is a certified ODE with certificate alpha(a) >= dphi(f(x,a)) + (id - lambda)(phi(x)) and phi(x) >= gamma(v(x)), where the input predicate alpha cannot depend on the state and id - lambda in K-infinity (lambda = 0 allowed).
work: Capucci & Myers (2026), arXiv:2604.03017; no DOI (preprint)
note: Validated against the paper in the 2026-10-29 validation log.

statement: Theorem 4.7 (LISS Lyapunov): the equilibrium of the open ODE is local ISS precisely when there is a differentiable local storage function phi and kappa1, kappa2 in K with kappa1(|a|) >= dphi(f(x,a)) + kappa2(phi(x)) for all a, x. Corollary 4.8: global if phi is radially unbounded.
work: Capucci & Myers (2026), arXiv:2604.03017; the paper's proof cites Sontag (2008), LNM 1932, DOI 10.1007/978-3-540-77653-6_3
note: The paper's proof is a citation of Sontag 2008 (its ref [33, Thm 3.4]). It credits the ISS notion itself to Sontag 1989 (ref [32]). Corrected in the validation log: the cited work is Sontag 2008, not Sontag 1989 and not Sontag-Wang.

statement: Sequential composition (Example 4.15): the lens s(m,o) = o, s#(m,o,a) = (a,m) certifies, with slack kappa from the inner (parallel-product) certificate (alpha1 + alpha2) pi2 <-> gamma1 + gamma2 to the outer (cascade) certificate alpha1 pi2 <-> gamma2; the slack condition is kappa(gamma1(m)) >= alpha2(m).
work: Capucci & Myers (2026), arXiv:2604.03017; no DOI (preprint)
note: Corrected form. The paper prints kappa(gamma1) >= alpha1 and glosses it as the first composee's assumption implying the second's. Substituting into eq (4.7) gives kappa(gamma1(m)) >= alpha2(m). This is the validator's reading, not confirmed with the authors; see the contradiction line for this item.

statement: Section 4.3: ISS preservation under composition needs (i) the composing lens's outer interface to carry a certificate of the form alpha pi2 (input-only assumption), and (ii) enough slack to pull through composition.
work: Capucci & Myers (2026), arXiv:2604.03017; no DOI (preprint)
note: Validated against Section 4.3 in the 2026-10-29 validation log.

statement: Sequential ISS composition is the only worked composite. The cascade assumption chain kappa(gamma1) >= alpha1 is a one-way implication, not a loop-gain condition; no feedback or small-gain theorem is derived.
work: Capucci & Myers (2026), arXiv:2604.03017; no DOI (preprint)
note: Negative scope of the paper, as read by 044 in Sections 1, 4.1-4.3, 5. Appendix A (monoidal double Grothendieck construction) was skimmed only, so a later loop result is unconfirmed (044 Unconfirmed).

statement: Forni-Sepulchre Theorem 2: Sigma1 and Sigma2 (strictly) uniformly differentially passive with the same tensor W, interconnected by u1 = -y2 + v1, u2 = y1 + v2, give an interconnection that is (strictly) uniformly differentially passive from v to y.
work: Forni, F., Sepulchre, R. (2013). On differentially dissipative dynamical systems. IFAC Proc. Vol. 46(23) 15-20, DOI 10.3182/20130904-3-FR-2041.00038; arXiv:1305.3456
note: Theorem statements read in 044 validation; proofs not checked. The feedback law u1 = -y2, u2 = +y1 is a skew coupling, which 044 flags as reciprocity in disguise (D028 territory, not pursued).

statement: Forni-Sepulchre Theorem 3: the Theorem 2 result without uniformity, with state-dependent W, gives differential storage S = S1 + S2.
note: Statement read; proof not checked.

statement: Forni-Sepulchre Theorem 4: with excess of output passivity and bounded trajectories, any two trajectories with the same input have outputs that converge, lim |y1(t) - y2(t)| = 0.
note: Statement read; proof not checked.

statement: Forni-Sepulchre Example 1 condition for x' = f(x) + g(x)u, y = h(x), with M(x) = d_xx m(x) and invertible Pi: M^T d_x[M f] <= 0, M g = Pi, d_x h^T W = M^T Pi. Example 2 extends this to outputs with feedthrough y = h(x) + i(x)u.
note: Corrected in validation: the conditions belong to Example 1, not Examples 1-2 (Example 2 is the feedthrough extension).

statement: The black-box functor from passive linear circuits to Lagrangian relations is symmetric monoidal and a hypergraph functor, and composition of circuits maps to composition of Lagrangian relations.
work: Baez, J. C., Fong, B. (2018). A compositional framework for passive linear networks. TAC 33, 1158-1222, DOI 10.70930/tac/zdyktmkc
note: Abstract and introduction read in 044; the 200k-character body was not read in full. The theorem is functoriality of black-boxing, not a stability or dissipation-inequality theorem.

statement: For resistor circuits the Lagrangian subspace is Graph(dQ), with Q the circuit's power functional.
work: Baez, J. C., Fong, B. (2018), TAC 33, 1158-1222, DOI 10.70930/tac/zdyktmkc
note: Checked in the text during validation.

statement: The class of passive linear circuits is closed under composition, and external behaviour of a composite is the composite of external behaviours.
work: Baez, J. C., Fong, B. (2018), TAC 33, 1158-1222, DOI 10.70930/tac/zdyktmkc
note: 044's reading of the seed. It holds for linear passive circuits only; nonlinear resistors, diodes and sources are excluded in the paper.

statement: Ames, Moeller, Tabuada Paper I: the existence of Lyapunov morphisms is necessary and sufficient for establishing the stability of flows.
work: Ames, A. D., Moeller, J., Tabuada, P. Categorical Lyapunov Theory I: Stability of Flows. Applied Categorical Structures 34(6) (2026), DOI 10.1007/s10485-026-09881-z; arXiv:2502.15276
note: Abstract only. Quote matches the abstract per the validation log. Concerns existence of Lyapunov morphisms, not composition along wiring diagrams.

statement: Shell well-posedness: the operadic wiring-diagram shell guarantees compositional totality and determinism, and Euler's method is functorial for undirected systems; the shell does not guarantee compositional stability of any kind.
work: Vagner, Spivak, Lerman (2015), TAC 30, 1793-1822, DOI 10.70930/tac/7tz1nkbd; Schultz, Spivak, Vasilakopoulou, ACS 28, DOI 10.1007/s10485-019-09565-x; Libkind, Baas, Patterson, Fairbanks (2022), EPTCS 372, 192-206, DOI 10.4204/eptcs.372.14
note: Based on keyword searches of the VSL and Libkind texts for stability terms (no hits except establish) and the SSV abstract ('totality and determinism compositionally'). The SSV claim rests on the abstract, which the validation log records.

statement: Passivity-type interconnection (Willems 1972; Moylan & Hill 1978): dissipative subsystems with supply rates s_i whose interconnection gives sum s_i <= 0 have sum V_i non-increasing on the loop; passivity is preserved by negative feedback and parallel interconnection.
note: Labelled [standard account] in 044; statements not re-read in this pass.

statement: Arcak 2007: strictly passive agents with a symmetric (reciprocal) interconnection coordinate.
note: Published abstract is not open; the statement rests on a seminar abstract, as in 040 §4c. Reciprocity is the cost.

statement: Jiang-Teel-Praly small-gain for feedback of ISS systems: the loop of gains satisfies gamma1 o gamma2 < id.
work: Jiang, Teel, Praly 1994, DOI 10.1007/bf01211469
note: Standard account; not re-read in 044. The linear special case (file 043 loop gain (c/a)^2 < 1 iff |c| < a) is consistent with it, per the cross-check.

statement: Dashkovskiy-Rüffer-Wirth (general networks): the gain operator is not amplifying around any cycle.
work: Dashkovskiy, Rüffer, Wirth 2007, DOI 10.1007/s00498-007-0014-8
note: Standard account; not re-read in 044. Matches 040's Gamma(s) not >= s.

statement: Parallel, series and (conditioned) feedback combinations of contracting systems are contracting.
work: Lohmiller & Slotine 1998, DOI 10.1016/s0005-1098(98)00019-3; Russo, di Bernardo, Sontag 2013, DOI 10.1109/tac.2012.2223355
note: Labelled [standard account] (Lohmiller-Slotine section 3) in 044; statements not re-read. 040 adds that skew-symmetric coupling is unconditional.

statement: Angulo-Slotine Theorem 1: the system x_i' = f_i(x,t) with a_ij = df_i/dx_j is contracting if (i) for reciprocal edges a_ji = -b_ij a_ij for some b_ij(x,t) > 0; (ii) a_ii = -alpha_i with alpha_i > (1/2) sum over feedback neighbours N_i of b_ij'/b_ij, where b_ij' is the time derivative; (iii) the graph has no cycles of length 3 or more.
note: Theorem 1 and Section IV extensions (delayed interconnections, modules) validated in 044. Proof not checked. For LTI functions the result reduces to the classical sign-stability criterion.

statement: Angulo-Slotine Corollary 1 (corrected form): if the asymmetries b_ij are constant, the system is contracting if a_ii < 0 and G has no cycle of length >= 3 (a sufficient condition).
note: Corrected in validation: the garbled 'iff-sufficiently' now reads 'if'. The condition needs the signs and cycle structure of the wiring, not the numerical gains.

statement: Kawano & Bullo (arXiv:2607.05640 v2): an incremental ISS-type bound on a control system is equivalent to an ISS-type bound on its variational system, and an infinitesimal contraction condition is equivalent to an incremental Lyapunov condition.
work: Kawano, Y., Bullo, F. Input-to-state stability implications in contraction theory. arXiv:2607.05640 (v2, 8 July 2026)
note: Abstract only read in 044. Not about composition; a possible route to a categorical contraction rule.

statement: Network motifs are overrepresented patterns; most arise from interconnections that best exploit the intrinsic stability characteristics of individual nodes, at node and module scale.
work: Angulo, Liu, Slotine (2015), Nature Physics 11(10) 848-852, DOI 10.1038/nphys3402; arXiv:1411.5412
note: Abstract only read. An observed overrepresentation of motifs, not an out-of-sample prediction or control result; no effect sizes are given in 044. Scale is node and module, not membership, group or crowd, so n/a.

statement: ISS, Definition 4.6: there exist kappa1, kappa2, kappa3 in K-infinity such that for every input a and trajectory x, |x(t,a)| <= kappa1(kappa2(|x(0)|) e^{-t}) + kappa3(||a||_inf) for all t >= 0.
work: Capucci & Myers (2026), arXiv:2604.03017; no DOI (preprint)
note: Definition read in 044 validation.

statement: Generalised Moore machine: state S, view v: S -> O, update u: S x I -> S, treated as a lens; a certified wiring diagram is a composite of certified lenses.
work: Capucci & Myers (2026), arXiv:2604.03017; no DOI (preprint)
note: Vocabulary read in Sections 1 and 4.1-4.3 of the paper.

statement: Setting for stability: axioms for doing Lyapunov theory in a category, with Lyapunov morphism defined into a reference system.
work: Ames, Moeller, Tabuada (2026), ACS 34(6), DOI 10.1007/s10485-026-09881-z; Ames, Mattenet, Moeller, arXiv:2505.22968
note: From abstracts only. The 044 'shape' point (a Lyapunov function as a morphism) is a translation, not a result of the papers.

statement: Monoidal setting (Ames II, Section 5, Definition 5.1): the monoidal structure is a laxator psi_{A,B}: FA x FB -> F(A x B), used to replace points with generalised elements so the category need not be concrete.
work: Ames, Mattenet, Moeller (2025), arXiv:2505.22968
note: Section 5 read in validation. Its purpose is removing concreteness, not parallel products; the earlier guess was withdrawn. Full-text keyword search found no wiring, interconnect, operad or lens.

statement: Passive linear circuit: a circuit whose components do not produce energy; batteries, current sources, nonlinear resistors and diodes are excluded.
work: Baez, J. C., Fong, B. (2018), TAC 33, 1158-1222, DOI 10.70930/tac/zdyktmkc
note: Checked in the text during validation ('not produce energy' and the exclusions). The engineering sense of passive, not the drive sense.

statement: Differential passivity: differential dissipativity lifts storage function and supply rate to the tangent bundle; with quadratic supply rates it gives supply Q = <delta y, delta u> with metric W_x.
note: Read in 044 (Definition 4, Theorems 2-4). The paper ties it to incremental stability as dissipativity is to stability (abstract).

statement: Reciprocal edges in a signed network: a_ji = -b_ij a_ij for some b_ij(x,t) > 0, so reciprocal interactions have opposite signs.
note: Condition (i) of Theorem 1, read in validation.

statement: Capucci-Myers Example 4.15 slack condition: printed kappa(gamma1) >= alpha1 vs derived kappa(gamma1(m)) >= alpha2(m) from eq (4.7).
work: Capucci & Myers (2026), arXiv:2604.03017; no DOI (preprint)
note: Side A: the paper prints kappa(gamma1) >= alpha1 and glosses it as the first composee's assumption implying the second's. Side B: substituting the lens into eq (4.7) gives alpha1(a) + kappa(gamma1(m)+gamma2(o)) >= alpha1(a) + alpha2(m), i.e. kappa(gamma1(m)) >= alpha2(m). Verdict: unresolved. The validator's reading is not confirmed against a later version or by the authors. Keep open.

statement: Attribution of the ISS cascade result: 044 says Sontag 2008 (ref [33] §4) vs 040 §5 credits the cascade result to Sontag under the 1989 citation.
note: Side A: the Capucci-Myers paper credits its ref [33, section 4], Sontag 2008. Side B: 040 §5 lists the cascade result under the 1989 citation. Verdict per 044: agree in substance (both Sontag); attribution of the first proof is unresolved from the files and was not checked at source. Keep open.

statement: Reading depth of Ames et al.: 044 table says 'Abstract only read' vs 044 §2 and the validation log say Section 5 of Paper II was read.
source: 044 Verdict table (top) vs 044 §2 and Validation log
work: Ames, Moeller, Tabuada (2026), DOI 10.1007/s10485-026-09881-z; Ames, Mattenet, Moeller, arXiv:2505.22968
note: Internal to 044, not cross-file. Side A: table cell 'abstract only read'. Side B: Section 5 read in validation and §2 agrees. Verdict in 044 (Cross-checks, row 3): the validation log is later and more specific, so the table cell is stale. Settled in favour of the log.

statement: Whether anyone has joined the shell and the certificate calculus: 044 narrows 040's 'No one has joined them for passivity or contraction' to ISS only, cascade case only.
source: 044 Cross-checks (Contradictions, row 1) vs 040 Summary and 'Does not exist'
work: Capucci & Myers (2026), arXiv:2604.03017 (ISS only); file 040 summary (no citation of its own)
note: 044's verdict: not a contradiction. 040 is scoped to passivity and contraction and was written before the 044 pass. Passivity and contraction stay open in both files. Read 040's gap sentence together with the 044 verdict. Keep open per the ledger rule for contradictions.

statement: The only motive is consistency: actors minimise deflection; no other drive is defined (one drive, consistency only)
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali (2016), Affect control processes, Artificial Intelligence 230, 134-172, doi:10.1016/j.artint.2015.09.004; preprint arXiv:1306.5279
note: Hoey et al. place ACT among psychological consistency theories [read, arXiv 1306.5279 §2.1]. The file says the 'no drive vocabulary beyond consistency' point is a gap for the algebra.

statement: Deflection D = ||f - tau||^2_W treated as a scalar potential on the state, whose gradient defines a pull (drive-reduction reading, compare Hull in file 16)
work: none; author's operator translation of the ACT potential, not a source claim
note: Author's own reading in §8, not sourced. Provenance sa, so it may not feed an equation.

statement: Identity inertia: a dynamics term xi(f', f, b_a, x) keeps an identity's fundamental f' near f, and on the agent's turn pulls it toward the agent's chosen behaviour b_a
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali (2016), Artificial Intelligence 230, 134-172, doi:10.1016/j.artint.2015.09.004; preprint arXiv:1306.5279 eq. (8)
note: A drive-like state inside the BayesACT dynamics, not a motive. Appendix simulation sets identity inertia beta_a = beta_c = 0.001 (ASR appendix, read).

statement: Emotion is a function of the transient impression of self and its difference from the fundamental identity sentiment (emotion as transient minus fundamental self-identity)
source: 045 §1 (Their vocabulary); §2 (Modifier and emotion equations); §4 (Model as stated)
work: Heise (2007), Expressive Order, Springer, doi:10.1007/978-0-387-38179-4 (per 03; not opened); cited via Hoey et al. ch. 14
note: Hoey et al. cite only Heise 2007 ch. 14 for the emotion equations, and the file says Heise 2007 itself was not opened. Other emotion attributions come from Wikipedia. Hoey's §4 also says states of Joy and other emotions would be functions of (f, tau).

statement: D = sum_i w_i (f_i - tau_i)^2, summed over the nine E, P, A components of actor, behaviour and object; w_i typically 1.0
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali (2016), Artificial Intelligence 230, 134-172, doi:10.1016/j.artint.2015.09.004; arXiv:1306.5279 eq. (1)
note: Troyer 2004 states the same definition [read]. Cross-check: 03 §2 matches this (weighted squared difference).

statement: tau' = M(x) G(f', tau, x), with M a 9 x 29 matrix of regression coefficients (rows E, P, A of actor, behaviour, object) and G a 29-vector of monomials in the previous transients tau and the new behaviour fundamental f_b'; x says whose turn it is (actor and object rows swapped on the other party's turn)
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali (2016), Artificial Intelligence 230, 134-172, doi:10.1016/j.artint.2015.09.004, §3.1.1; arXiv:1306.5279
size_dependence: Coefficients are estimated per culture and per gender (equation families, see the coefficient-families line)
note: Cross-check: 03 §2 describes the same nine-regression map; 06 flags ACT as operators with equations. Cited form is G as a non-linear operator (validated against arXiv 1306.5279v2).

statement: G (29 entries, Hoey eq. (3), rewriting of Heise 2007 eq. (11.16)) = 1; tau_ae, tau_ap, tau_aa; f_be, f_bp, f_ba; tau_ce, tau_cp, tau_ca; then 15 two-way products and 4 three-way products (including tau_ae tau_ce f_be and tau_ap tau_ca f_bp)
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali (2016), eq. (3), arXiv:1306.5279; Heise (2007) eq. (11.16), Expressive Order (not opened)
note: Layout caveat: the PDF extraction scrambled the layout, so the order of some middle terms must be re-checked against the paper before coding. The count of 29 and degree-3 monomials are stated explicitly in the source.

statement: A_e' = c1 A_e + c2 A_p + c3 A_a + c4 B_e + c5 B_p + c6 B_a + c7 O_e + c8 O_p + c9 O_a + c10 A_a B_e + ... + c27 A_e B_p O_p + c28 A_p B_p O_a + e (28 coefficients, no constant term; ellipsis elides c11..c26, see source)
work: Troyer, L. (2004), Affect Control Theory as a Foundation for Socially Intelligent Systems, AAAI Spring Symposium SS-04-02; https://cdn.aaai.org/Symposia/Spring/2004/SS-04-02/SS04-02-026.pdf; attributed there to Smith-Lovin (1987), doi:10.1080/0022250x.1987.9990026
note: Transcription checked against the PDF in validation. Source lists B_a O_e twice (c11 and c22), so 27 distinct terms as printed (see contradictions). Troyer does not print coefficient values; they are published elsewhere (see the actdata line).

statement: tau' = H(tau, x) f_b' - C(tau, x), with H a 9 x 3 and C a 9 x 1 matrix; the map is linear in the behaviour's fundamental f_b' once tau and x are fixed
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali (2016), Artificial Intelligence 230, 134-172, doi:10.1016/j.artint.2015.09.004, §3.1.1 (equation after eq. (4)); arXiv:1306.5279
note: Linearity holds only in the behaviour term. The map as a whole is a degree-3 polynomial in the transient state, so it is not linear in state.

statement: Optimal behaviour: minimising D over f_b' is a quadratic minimisation, a linear least-squares solve; in Hoey's notation f_b* = -z^{-1}[-H_a(f_a - C_a - ...) - H_c(f_c - C_c - ...) - z C_b (1 - H_b)^{-1}], with z = H_a^T H_a + (I - H_b)^T(I - H_b) + H_c^T H_c
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali (2016), appendix B, eq. (46), arXiv:1306.5279; matches Heise (2007) eq. (12.21), Expressive Order (not opened)
note: Block layout reconstructed from a scrambled extraction, so check against the PDF before coding. Interact finds the dictionary behaviour nearest the continuous optimum, so predictions are limited to rated words. Hoey et al. warn of constraints on the action space.

statement: Heise (2007) closed forms for the optimal actor and object identities: eqs. (13.11) and (13.18)
work: Heise (2007), Expressive Order, Springer, doi:10.1007/978-0-387-38179-4 (per 03; not opened)
note: Claim read as stated by Hoey et al. (tagged [read, via Hoey et al.] in the file); Heise 2007 itself not opened.

statement: Affect control principle: actors work to experience transient impressions consistent with their fundamental sentiments (equivalently, choose behaviour and labels to minimise deflection)
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali (2016), Definition 1, Artificial Intelligence 230, 134-172, doi:10.1016/j.artint.2015.09.004; arXiv:1306.5279
note: A stated principle, not a derived equation. The Interact rule of thumb for who acts next is a separate line.

statement: Interact rule of thumb: the person whose optimal action yields the lowest deflection acts next (guide example deflections 0.87, 1.19, 1.27)
work: Heise, Interact guide (PDF mirrored at cs.uwaterloo.ca ACT mirror); no DOI
size_dependence: Applies to dyadic turn-taking; groups beyond dyads handled only by each interactant applying the same rule (045 §8)
note: A rule of thumb in the software documentation, not a tested prediction. Validated against the guide.

statement: BayesACT transient dynamics (eq. 5): Pr(tau' | tau, f', x) = delta(tau' - H(tau, x) f_b' - C(tau, x)), deterministic
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali (2016), Artificial Intelligence 230, 134-172, doi:10.1016/j.artint.2015.09.004; arXiv:1306.5279 eq. (5)
note: Validated against arXiv 1306.5279 eqs. (5), (7), (8), (13), (18) in validation.

statement: BayesACT deflection potential (eq. 7, corrected form): phi(f', tau') proportional to exp(-(f' - tau')^T Sigma^{-1} (f' - tau')); with Sigma diagonal with elements 1/w_i, log phi = -D + c, where D is eq. (1)
source: 045 §4 (Model as stated); validation log and Contradictions in §10-§11
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali (2016), Artificial Intelligence 230, 134-172, doi:10.1016/j.artint.2015.09.004; arXiv:1306.5279 eq. (7)
note: Corrected form. The source text says log phi = D + c, but eq. (7) as printed gives -D + c, so the potential is highest at zero deflection. Sign slip inherited from Hoey et al.; corrected in validation.

statement: BayesACT fundamental dynamics (eqs. 8, 18): Pr(f' | f, tau, x, b_a, phi) proportional to exp(-psi(f', tau, x) - xi(f', f, b_a, x)), with psi = (f' - M G)^T Sigma^{-1} (f' - M G)
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali (2016), Artificial Intelligence 230, 134-172, doi:10.1016/j.artint.2015.09.004; arXiv:1306.5279 eqs. (8), (18)
note: xi is the inertia term (see the identity-inertia drive line).

statement: Expected deflection under belief b(s): E_b[D] = integral of b(s) D(s) ds
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali (2016), Artificial Intelligence 230, 134-172, doi:10.1016/j.artint.2015.09.004; arXiv:1306.5279 eq. (13)
note: Used for planning under a POMDP with reward on top of the potential; beliefs via sequential Monte Carlo (file §4).

statement: Coefficient families: Interact carries separate impression-formation equation sets for U.S.A. 1978, Japan 1984, Canada 1985, China 2000 and Germany 2007 (menu), with male and female sets; ABO equations were 'obtained in two phases' and ABOS equations come from stepwise regression
work: Heise, Interact guide, 'Changing Cultures' and 'Impression-formation Equations' pages and footnote 5 (cs.uwaterloo.ca ACT mirror); no DOI
size_dependence: Equations differ by culture, gender and decade; the guide notes methodological differences in estimation may change results
note: The guide also says U.S. 1970s equations are used for Irish and Chinese analyses and German 2007 for Germany. Hoey et al. say impression-formation equations exist for English, Japanese and German. Which set Hoey et al. used is not stated.

statement: Published coefficient sets (validation correction): actdata holds nine equation sets (nc1978, japan1984, canada1985, canada20012003, china2000, germany2007, us2010, egypt2014, morocco2015), each with impressionabo, impressionabos, selfdir, traitid, emotionid, male and female files; example us2010 ABO male constant row Z000000000 -0.16 -0.06 -0.05 -0.26 0.09 0.21 -0.18 0.00 -0.14
source: 045 §2 (Troyer's printed example, corrected in validation); §10; Unconfirmed
work: github.com/ahcombs/actdata (Aidan Combs, R package, data-raw/eqns/, CC0-1.0); also Interact's 'View equations' screen (Heise, guide, 'Handling Equations')
size_dependence: Per culture and gender
note: Corrected from an earlier claim that the coefficients were unpublished. Interact-format files, one row per term with a 0/1 string over Ae Ap Aa Be Bp Ba Oe Op Oa. Licence CC0-1.0 on the package conflicts with the guide's noncommercial terms (see contradictions).

statement: Modifier and emotion equations: emotion and social-identity amalgamation impressions are predicted by empirically derived equations (Averett & Heise 1987; Heise & Thomas 1989)
work: Averett & Heise (1987), Modified social identities, J. Math. Sociol. 13, 103-132, doi:10.1080/0022250x.1987.9990028; Heise & Thomas (1989), Predicting impressions created by combinations of emotion and social identity, Social Psychology Quarterly 52, 141-, doi:10.2307/2786913
note: Neither paper was opened; attribution of these equations is from Wikipedia. Hoey et al. cite only Heise 2007 ch. 14 for emotion equations. Provenance sa, so these may not feed an equation.

statement: Hoey et al.: 'many experimental and observational studies have shown that deflection is indeed inversely related to the likelihood of humans to engage in the corresponding social actions'
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali (2016), Artificial Intelligence 230, 134-172, doi:10.1016/j.artint.2015.09.004; arXiv:1306.5279
size_dependence: Three named studies are small-group leadership, dyadic non-verbal displays and small-group turn-taking
note: Scale is the extractor's assignment from the three studies below, not stated in the file. No effect sizes, out-of-sample accuracy or independent replication found. The three named studies are all by ACT authors or collaborators.

statement: Schröder & Scholl (2009): mock leaders in a computer-simulated business game; verbal behaviours consistent with deflection minimisation
work: Schröder & Scholl (2009), Affective dynamics of leadership: an experimental test of ACT, Social Psychology Quarterly 72, 180-197, doi:10.1177/019027250907200207
note: Citation-level only; paper not opened. No effect sizes read. Consistency with deflection minimisation is Hoey et al.'s characterisation.

statement: Schröder, Netzel, Schermuly & Scholl (2013): culture-constrained affective consistency of non-verbal displays in dyads, consistent with deflection minimisation
work: Schröder, Netzel, Schermuly & Scholl (2013), Culture-constrained affective consistency of interpersonal behavior, Social Psychology 44, 47-58, doi:10.1027/1864-9335/a000101
size_dependence: Dyadic; culture-constrained
note: Scale is the extractor's assignment (dyadic interpersonal behaviour), not stated in the file. Citation-level only; paper not opened.

statement: Heise (2013): conversational turn-taking in small groups consistent with deflection minimisation
work: Heise (2013), Modeling interactions in small groups, Social Psychology Quarterly 76, 52-72, doi:10.1177/0190272512467654
size_dependence: Small groups
note: Citation-level only; paper not opened. The file says the turn-taking evidence is per Hoey et al.

statement: BayesACT MathTutor pilot (Hoey et al. §4.2.1, Table 2): 20 participants (7 female), 10 per arm, about 20 minutes, one-tailed t-tests df = 18, p < .05 to < .01; BayesAct tutor vs control tutor choosing affective action at random from the same set; mean deflection 2.9 ± 2.1 (BayesAct) vs 4.5 ± 2.2 (random)
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali (2016), Artificial Intelligence 230, 134-172, doi:10.1016/j.artint.2015.09.004, §4.2.1 and Table 2; arXiv:1306.5279
size_dependence: Small sample (n = 20); a 37-participant survey (22 female) built the tutoring system's EPA mappings; Hoey et al. say to treat the result with caution
note: Scale: dyadic tutoring, no scale assigned in the file. Ethics: extractor's classification, since the file does not address it. The tutor's affective choices steer the student's impressions, and the file does not mention consent. Items included 'dialogue was simple and natural'. No out-of-sample test.

statement: BayesACT simulations: agents recover identities with low identity deflection over sample counts, tolerate noise, and track a shifting client (Appendix C tables)
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali (2016), Artificial Intelligence 230, 134-172, doi:10.1016/j.artint.2015.09.004; arXiv:1306.5279 Appendix C
note: Simulation by the model's authors, not human data. The file found no evidence that BayesACT behaviour predictions were tested against naturally occurring interaction data.

statement: Troyer (2004) simulations: relabelled and responded to deflections of 2.0, 5.0, 7.0, then 12.0 or 14.0 (grouch with scold; delinquent with avoid)
work: Troyer (2004), AAAI Spring Symposium SS-04-02, Table 2; https://cdn.aaai.org/Symposia/Spring/2004/SS-04-02/SS04-02-026.pdf
note: Simulation outputs. Troyer's pilot measured only EPA ratings of computer terms and ran Interact simulations; it tested nothing against behaviour.

statement: Deflection corresponds to the perceived likelihood of an event (Heise & MacKinnon 1987, as attributed by Troyer)
work: Heise & MacKinnon (1987), Affective bases of likelihood judgments, J. Math. Sociol. 13, 133-151, doi:10.1080/0022250x.1987.9990029
note: Tagged [read, secondary]: read via Troyer's statement. The original article was not opened; the reprint DOI doi:10.4324/9781315025773-5 is a 2016 reprint. No effect sizes.

statement: Within-culture agreement on EPA is high across subgroups, and cultural means from as few as a few dozen respondents are 'extremely stable over extended periods' (Heise 2010)
work: Heise (2010), Surveying Cultures, Wiley, doi:10.1002/9780470575789; as cited by Hoey et al.
size_dependence: Few dozen respondents per culture
note: Read as a claim in Hoey et al.; the underlying statistics were not seen by the file's author.

statement: No independent meta-analysis or independent test of deflection minimisation as a predictor of behaviour was found; no quantitative predictive standing (how often the minimum-deflection behaviour is the one chosen) is reported in anything read
work: none; author's search finding
note: Not re-tested in validation: the shared web-search budget was exhausted. The file says treat it as the original author's negative finding, unverified.

statement: Fundamental sentiment f: the culturally shared EPA (evaluation, potency, activity) meaning of a concept, a point in R^3
work: Heise, Interact guide (cs.uwaterloo.ca mirror); Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali arXiv:1306.5279 §2.1
size_dependence: Per culture and per gender
note: Cross-check: 03 §2 has the same two-layer structure.

statement: Transient impression tau: the momentary EPA meaning of an element (actor, behaviour, object) after an event; the 9-vector tau holds E, P, A for each of the three elements
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali arXiv:1306.5279 §3.1.1
note: Cross-check: 03 §2 has the same two layers. Troyer's regressors are pre-event impressions, which for a first event equal fundamentals.

statement: ABO event: actor-behaviour-object, extended with setting and modifier (ABOS); operands are concepts (identities, behaviours, modifiers, settings), each a point in R^3 (EPA)
work: Heise, Interact guide (cs.uwaterloo.ca mirror); no DOI
size_dependence: Dyadic actor-object core; setting and modifier added
note: Cross-check: 03 §2 has the same event grammar.

statement: Deflection is an unbounded sum of squares, not a 0-1 quantity: the Interact guide's worked event has deflection 4.3 in the lowest of its four quarter-sectors (comfortable/normal, unusual, weird, invalidates the impression)
work: Heise, Interact guide (cs.uwaterloo.ca mirror); no DOI
note: Interact reports total deflection and the parts from stressing the actor's identity and the object's identity; the remainder comes from behaviour and setting.

statement: Reidentification: relabelling an actor (or the other) to reduce deflection when behaviour cannot resolve it (e.g. 'grouch', 'delinquent')
work: Troyer (2004), AAAI Spring Symposium SS-04-02; https://cdn.aaai.org/Symposia/Spring/2004/SS-04-02/SS04-02-026.pdf
note: Also called attribution in the file's vocabulary list. In §8 relabelling is a second operator: the nearest identity to the arg-min.

statement: EPA dictionary (repository): per-culture, per-gender mean E, P, A ratings of rated concepts (identities, behaviours, modifiers, settings), with standard deviations in Interact; 18 datasets listed for simulation in Interact across USA, Canada, China, Egypt, Germany, Japan, Morocco, Northern Ireland and France/Germany
work: affectcontroltheory.org/resources-for-researchers/data-sets-for-simulation/ (hub); Francis & Heise (Indiana 2003); Schneider (West Germany 1989)
size_dependence: Per culture and gender; a word can carry different EPA across cultures (Japanese child male -0.24, -2.10, 2.75; American child rated very positively)
note: Free for noncommercial research use only (guide terms). Indiana 2003: 500 identities, 500 behaviours, 300 modifiers, 200 settings. West Germany 1989: 442 identities, 295 behaviours, 67 modifiers. Rater counts disagree; see contradictions.

statement: EPA scale range: -4.3 to +4.3 (Hoey et al. §2.1) versus -4.5 to +4.5 (Troyer 2004)
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali arXiv:1306.5279 §2.1; Troyer (2004), AAAI Spring Symposium SS-04-02
note: Side A: Hoey et al. -4.3..+4.3. Side B: Troyer -4.5..+4.5. The file calls it a convention difference between sources, and the Interact guide's example profiles are consistent with either. Verdict: unresolved, status open.

statement: Equation-family dating for Canada and Japan: the guide's menu lists 1978, 1984, 1985, 2000, 2007, while its running text says 1990s Canadian and Japanese equations
work: Heise, Interact guide, equation-culture menu and running text (cs.uwaterloo.ca mirror); actdata (github.com/ahcombs/actdata)
note: Side A: menu (canada1985, japan1984). Side B: running text '1990s'. Partly resolved in validation: the actdata files are labelled canada1985 and japan1984, matching the menu, and the guide's Cultures page dates Canadian data to the mid-1980s, so the 1990s text looks like the error. Japan not settled, since the Japanese ratings run 1989-1996 on that page. Status open for Japan.

statement: Rater counts for two dictionaries: Indiana 2003 has N = 1,027 (hub page) versus 970 (guide, 496 female, 474 male); West Germany 1989 has N = 520 (hub) versus 400 Mannheim students (guide)
source: 045 §5 (Details for the two pages opened); Unconfirmed; validation log
work: affectcontroltheory.org dictionary pages (Indiana 2003; West Germany 1989); Heise, Interact guide Cultures page (cs.uwaterloo.ca mirror)
note: Side A: hub, 1,027 and 520. Side B: guide, 970 and 400. Possibly before and after exclusions. Verdict: unresolved.

statement: Dataset count: the Interact guide describes 'eleven cultural repositories' (six lacking setting sentiments) against the hub's list of 18 datasets
work: Heise, Interact guide history (cs.uwaterloo.ca mirror); affectcontroltheory.org data-sets page
note: Side A: guide's older count of eleven. Side B: hub's newer list of 18. Verdict: unresolved, likely older versus newer count.

statement: Troyer's equation versus Hoey's G: the file first said Troyer's A, B, O are fundamental ratings while Hoey uses transients, and that the regression structure is the same; validation found the shape is the same (constant and linear terms plus selected two- and three-way products, 28 non-constant terms each) but the term sets differ
source: 045 §2 (Troyer's printed example, corrected in validation); validation log
work: Troyer (2004), AAAI Spring Symposium SS-04-02; Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali arXiv:1306.5279 eq. (3)
note: Side A: 'same regression, fundamental vs transient' (earlier file text). Side B: different estimations and different term sets (for example Troyer has A_a B_e, A_e B_a, A_a B_a O_a; Hoey's G has tau_ae tau_ce and tau_ae tau_cp, absent from Troyer). Verdict: the contrast was false and the sameness overstated; do not treat as one canonical term set (resolved).

statement: BayesACT deflection potential sign: the paper's text says log phi = D + c, but its eq. (7) as printed gives log phi = -D + c
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali (2016), Artificial Intelligence 230, 134-172, doi:10.1016/j.artint.2015.09.004; arXiv:1306.5279 eq. (7) and text
note: Side A: text, log phi = D + c. Side B: eq. (7), log phi = -D + c. Verdict: -D + c, the potential is highest at zero deflection (resolved in validation; the source's sign slip).

statement: Troyer's printed equation lists the term B_a O_e twice (as c11 and c22), so as printed it has 27 distinct non-constant terms rather than 28
work: Troyer (2004), AAAI Spring Symposium SS-04-02, transient-evaluation equation
note: Side A: 28 coefficients as numbered. Side B: 27 distinct terms. Verdict: a typo in Troyer, not in this file (resolved).

statement: Coefficient availability: the file first said the published, tabulated coefficients for the impression-formation map did not exist; validation found them public in Interact's 'View equations' screen and in the actdata package
source: 045 §9 (Does not exist, struck); §10; Unconfirmed (M, struck in validation)
work: Heise, Interact guide, 'Handling Equations' (cs.uwaterloo.ca mirror); github.com/ahcombs/actdata (CC0-1.0)
note: Side A: earlier 'not published'. Side B: published in machine-readable form. Verdict: the later claim is correct (resolved). Which set Hoey et al. used is still not stated in what was read.

statement: Event-map linearity: the file 32 §4 says events change EPA by 'a linear transformation function', while 045 §2 and 03 §2 describe a degree-3 polynomial map in the transient state, linear only in the new behaviour's own EPA
work: Hoey, Schröder & Alhothali arXiv:1306.5279v2 (G is a non-linear operator; M is a 9 x 29 matrix); Troyer (2004) prints products up to three-way
note: Side A: file 32, linear. Side B: files 045 and 03, polynomial. Verdict: 045 and 03 right, 32 wrong (primary source re-checked in the cross-check). 32 should read 'a fitted non-linear (polynomial) map' with linearity only in the behaviour term (resolved).

statement: Licence of the coefficient and dictionary data: actdata is CC0-1.0, while the Interact guide's terms make site materials copyrighted by Heise/Indiana for noncommercial research use only, with governmental, political or commercial use requiring written permission
work: github.com/ahcombs/actdata (CC0-1.0); Heise, Interact guide terms of use (cs.uwaterloo.ca mirror)
note: Side A: CC0 package licence. Side B: noncommercial research terms on the guide's materials. Verdict: unresolved. For a public repo of these data, ask rather than assume; private noncommercial use is permitted.

statement: German equation source: the guide cites a 2007 German equation set by Schröder ('Germany 2007'), which is not on the hub's dataset list; the hub lists West Germany 1989 as the German dictionary
work: Heise, Interact guide (cs.uwaterloo.ca mirror); affectcontroltheory.org data-sets page
note: Side A: 2007 equations via the guide. Side B: 1989 dictionary via the hub. Verdict: unresolved; the 2007 data may be the source of the equations and the 1989 dictionary the one shown.

statement: Heise (2007) Expressive Order DOI: the file says it was not opened and no DOI was checked, while file 03 records doi:10.1007/978-0-387-38179-4 as Crossref-confirmed
work: Heise (2007), Expressive Order, Springer; doi:10.1007/978-0-387-38179-4 (per 03)
note: Side A: 045, no DOI checked. Side B: 03, Crossref-confirmed DOI. Verdict: take the DOI from 03; the book itself is still not opened here (open).

statement: T (action tendency): inertial state; "a wish persists until satisfied and does not increase unless instigated"
work: Revelle 2008 draft, Cues, Tendencies and Actions (https://personality-project.org/revelle/publications/cta.pdf; no DOI); Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740; Atkinson & Birch 1970, The Dynamics of Action, Wiley (no DOI; book not read)
note: Definition quoted in Revelle 2008 Table 1 [read]. The book itself was not read; implementers only.

statement: F (instigating force): rate at which the stimulus situation raises an action tendency
work: Revelle 2008 draft (https://personality-project.org/revelle/publications/cta.pdf; no DOI); Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740
note: Vocabulary from Revelle 2008 Table 1 and Blankenship et al. 1995.

statement: c (consummatory value): how fast doing the activity satisfies the action tendency (doughnut > celery)
work: Revelle 2008 draft (https://personality-project.org/revelle/publications/cta.pdf; no DOI); Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740
note: The doughnut/celery example is from Blankenship et al. 1995 and Revelle 2008 Table 1.

statement: C (consummatory force): the outflow applied to T, only while the activity is going (ongoing)
work: Revelle 2008 draft (https://personality-project.org/revelle/publications/cta.pdf; no DOI); Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740
note: Whether C = c·T (Revelle Eq. 2) or C = c·BAR-T is unresolved; see contradiction 1.

statement: I (inhibitory force): rate at which the stimulus situation raises the negaction tendency
work: Revelle 2008 draft (https://personality-project.org/revelle/publications/cta.pdf; no DOI); Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740
note: Vocabulary from Revelle 2008 Table 1 and Blankenship et al. 1995.

statement: N (negaction tendency): the "tendency not to"; "opposes, resists, and dampens the effect of an action tendency"
work: Atkinson & Birch 1970 p. 204, quoted in Slade & Rush 1991, doi:10.1037/0022-3514.60.1.165; Revelle 2008 draft; Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740
note: The quotation is second-hand: taken from Slade & Rush, who quote the book's p. 204. The book was not read.

statement: r (resistance value): cost of resisting that activity
work: Revelle 2008 draft (https://personality-project.org/revelle/publications/cta.pdf; no DOI); Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740
note: Parameter, not a state; listed because the file names it alongside the forces.

statement: R (force of resistance): outflow of N, written R = r·N (Revelle Eq. 5) or R = r·min(T, N) (Blankenship et al., citing A&B 1970 p. 239)
work: Revelle 2008 draft (https://personality-project.org/revelle/publications/cta.pdf; no DOI); Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740
note: Two forms conflict; see contradiction 2. The file says the min form is the better-attested one.

statement: selective attention: a number in (0,1) that scales the instigating and inhibitory forces of a non-focal stimulus (the file's example: full 100% forces of the doughnut are not applied)
work: Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740
note: Appears in Blankenship et al. 1995 only, not in Revelle's CTA draft.

statement: N_ach and N_af (approach and avoidance motives), entering as F = Ps(1-Ps)·N_ach and I = Ps(1-Ps)·N_af, with Ps as the file writes it
work: Revelle & Condon 2015 draft (Eqs. 7-8), doi:10.1016/j.jrp.2014.12.006; Atkinson 1957, doi:10.1037/h0043445
note: Revelle Eqs 7-8 are tagged [read] in the file. Ps is not defined in the file. The 2015 draft is marked not to be cited; the published version was not checked.

statement: CTA state variables: cue vector C (set by the environment), tendency vector T, and action vector A, with T and A dynamic
work: Revelle 2008 draft (Eqs. 10-13); Revelle & Condon 2015 draft, doi:10.1016/j.jrp.2014.12.006 (Eqs. 10-11)
note: A is the replacement for A&B's negaction-based state in CTA; the file counts this as the main structural change.

statement: inhibitory cue: a cue that gives a negative tendency, or an inhibitory entry in the matrix i
work: Revelle 2008 draft (Fig. 5); Revelle & Condon 2015 draft, doi:10.1016/j.jrp.2014.12.006
note: The delay-not-prevent behaviour of Fig. 5 is simulation output only.

statement: fear of failure: the inhibitory motive of the model as tested in achievement-task latency studies, high versus low groups
work: Blankenship 1987, doi:10.1037/0022-3514.53.2.361 (not read); Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740
note: Second-hand from Blankenship et al. 1995 and Revelle & Condon 2015; primary not read. Framing is the file's own.

statement: dT_i/dt = F_i - C_i, with C_i = c_i·T_i if activity i is ongoing and C_i = 0 otherwise; so dT/dt = F - cT if ongoing, F if not
work: Revelle 2008 draft, Eq. 3 (https://personality-project.org/revelle/publications/cta.pdf; no DOI); Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740
note: Uses C = c·T (Revelle Eq. 2). Blankenship's C = c·BAR-T would change it; see contradiction 1. Not the book's form, which is unconfirmed.

statement: dN_i/dt = I_i - R_i = I_i - r_i·N_i, at all times, whether or not activity i is ongoing
work: Revelle 2008 draft, Eq. 5 (https://personality-project.org/revelle/publications/cta.pdf; no DOI); Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740
note: Revelle: "it requires effort to resist even if not doing a task". Blankenship agrees N acts at all times but programmes R = r·min(T, N) (contradiction 2).

statement: Discrete time as implemented: ΔT = F - C and ΔN = I - R per time unit
work: Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740
note: Implementation of the continuous equations. The file notes FORTRAN versions from 1973 onward, cited only as named in Blankenship et al.

statement: Switching rule: the dominant activity is argmax over i of T_i - N_i (ties broken by listed order); in the simplest case an activity is ongoing when it is dominant, and only its consummatory force is switched on
work: Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740 (STELLA dominance code); Revelle 2008 draft (Atkinson & Birch 'assumed that action choice ... followed the maximum action tendency')
note: The max-selection form is Blankenship's implementation. The file reads the 1970 book's rule second-hand only. Revelle's CTA has no max rule in its dynamics (contradiction 5).

statement: Consummatory force is applied only after the activity has been dominant for an initiation lag, and continues for a cessation lag after it stops being dominant
work: Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740 (lag of 10 time units in their example); Revelle 2008 draft (also describes lags)
note: Purpose per the file: separate just coming on or going off, avoid quick reversals (behavioural chatter). PASE page, not read in full, gives 2-5; the book's lag values are unconfirmed (§8).

statement: Ongoing asymptote: T∞ = F/c (with C = c·T)
work: Revelle 2008 draft, Eq. 4 (https://personality-project.org/revelle/publications/cta.pdf; no DOI)
note: Under C = c·(T - N) the asymptote differs: T → F/c + N, so the resultant T - N → F/c (contradiction 1).

statement: Closed-form trajectories (derived): ongoing T(t) = F/c + (T0 - F/c)·e^(-ct); not ongoing T(t) = T0 + F·t; N(t) = I/r + (N0 - I/r)·e^(-rt) always
work: Derived in 046 from Revelle 2008 Eqs 1-5 (no published source states these trajectories)
note: [derived] in the file, not tagged [read]. Per the schema, provenance is sa. Revelle gives only the asymptotes.

statement: Inhibition delays but does not prevent activity: an inhibitory cue delays onset of an activity with an instigating stimulus without suppressing it
work: Revelle 2008 draft, Fig. 5 (https://personality-project.org/revelle/publications/cta.pdf; no DOI); Slade & Rush 1991, doi:10.1037/0022-3514.60.1.165 (paraphrasing Atkinson & Birch 1970 pp. 232-233 and 1974 pp. 297-301)
note: Tagged [read as a claim]. Fig. 5 is a CTA simulation. The 'no matter how strong' sentence is Slade & Rush's paraphrase, not a quotation of A&B. The file calls this the only theorem-shaped result of the model.

statement: Latency bound (derived, under R = r·N): N is bounded by max(N0, I/r), so T - N exceeds any baseline b after t ≤ (b - T0 + max(N0, I/r))/F; the onset-latency bound is linear in I/r and inversely proportional to F
work: Derived in 046 from Revelle 2008 Eq. 5 form
note: Derived, not tagged [read]; per schema provenance is sa. Depends on R = r·N; does not survive R = r·min(T, N) (next line).

statement: Under R = r·min(T, N) (derived): while T < N, d(T - N)/dt = F - I + r·T, which turns positive once T > (I - F)/r, reached in finite time; the no-suppression conclusion survives, the latency bound does not
work: Derived in 046 from Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740 (min form, citing Atkinson & Birch 1970 p. 239)
note: [derived]. Added in validation correction (the min form had been omitted from the file).

statement: No absorbing activity (derived): if at least two activities have F > 0, the ongoing activity's T is bounded by max(T0, F/c) while each idle activity has T - N → ∞, so every idle activity eventually overtakes
work: Derived in 046 from the equations of Revelle 2008 and Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740
note: Consistent with 'stream of behaviour' (Atkinson & Birch as quoted by Blankenship et al.) and 'change of behavior even in a constant environment' (Revelle 2008, read). The theorem itself is derived, not quoted.

statement: Chatter condition (derived): at a switch from i to j, T_r,i = T_r,j; afterward j's resultant slope is F_j - c_j·T_j - (I_j - r_j·N_j) and i's is F_i - (I_i - r_i·N_i); reversal happens at once iff j's slope is smaller
work: Derived in 046 from Revelle 2008 and Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740
note: Verbal account of chatter and of why lags were added is read in Revelle and Blankenship et al.; the algebra is derived.

statement: Static limit (derived): with F = Ps(1-Ps)·N_ach and I = Ps(1-Ps)·N_af, the asymptotic resultant is (N_ach/c - N_af/r)·Ps(1-Ps)
work: Derived in 046 from Revelle & Condon 2015 draft Eqs. 7-8, doi:10.1016/j.jrp.2014.12.006
note: Recovers Atkinson 1957's form only if c = r = 1 or the same scale is imposed on both sides (the file's proviso, which 16 §6 omits).

statement: Atkinson 1957 resultant: T_r = (N_ach - N_af)·Ps(1-Ps)
work: Atkinson 1957, Psychological Review 64(6), 359-372, doi:10.1037/h0043445 (not read)
note: Equations come from Revelle's handout and CTA paper, not the 1957 paper itself. Authorship, venue and pages verified via Crossref.

statement: Carry-over (Revelle & Michaels 1976): success quenches T (consummation) but failure does not, so the resultant tendency grows over successive failures, faster for harder tasks
work: Revelle & Michaels 1976, Psychological Review 83(5), 394-404, doi:10.1037/0033-295x.83.5.394 (not read)
note: Tagged [read] from Revelle's handout and CTA draft; the 1976 paper itself not read. Reconciles Atkinson's inverted-U with Locke's monotone goal-difficulty effect.

statement: CTA dynamics: dT/dt = s·C - c·A; dA/dt = e·T - i·A (C cues, T tendencies, A actions; s, e, c, i matrices)
work: Revelle 2008 draft, Eqs. 10-13 (https://personality-project.org/revelle/publications/cta.pdf; no DOI); Revelle & Condon 2015 draft, doi:10.1016/j.jrp.2014.12.006, Eqs. 10-11
note: Diagonal of i is the cost of doing the action; off-diagonals mutual incompatibility (see definition 'CTA inhibition matrix').

statement: CTA asymptotes, corrected (scalar case): A∞ = s·C/c and T∞ = i·s·C/(e·c); Revelle's printed Eqs 12-13 (T∞ = s·C·i/c, A∞ = e·C/c) are wrong unless s = e = 1
work: Derived from Revelle 2008 draft Eqs 10-13 (https://personality-project.org/revelle/publications/cta.pdf; no DOI); simulated in 046
note: Corrected form, as the validation log records it. Simulation: with s = e = 0.05, c = 0.03, i = 0.1, C = 3, A reaches 100.0 = C/c. Consequence: asymptotic action is independent of e and i. Derived and simulated, not tagged [read].

statement: Characteristic polynomial of the scalar linear CTA system: λ² + i·λ + e·c = 0; damped oscillator when i² < 4ec
work: Derived in 046 from Revelle 2008 draft Eqs 10-13 (https://personality-project.org/revelle/publications/cta.pdf; no DOI)
note: Re-derived in validation. Explains the damped waves in Revelle's Figs 1 and 3. Derived, not tagged [read].

statement: Resultant action tendency: T_r,i = T_i - N_i, the quantity compared between activities
work: Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740 (called BAR-T); Revelle 2008 draft (https://personality-project.org/revelle/publications/cta.pdf; no DOI)
note: Blankenship's term is BAR-T. Its definition as T minus N is read.

statement: Displacement: a stimulus instigating one activity also feeds the instigating force of an associated activity, applied in every state and scaled by selective attention when the stimulus is non-focal
work: Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740
note: Their example adds 0.2 × the doughnut's force of 2.0 to the milk's force of 1.0, with selective attention 0.6. Validation corrected an earlier misdescription (the displaced force applies in every state).

statement: Substitution: consummatory force is shared among related activities (eating the doughnut also satisfies the tendency to eat a sticky bun)
work: Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740
note: Lifted by the full model into off-diagonal couplings in CTA's matrices, per the file.

statement: CTA inhibition matrix i: the diagonal is the cost of doing the action; off-diagonals are mutual incompatibility; mutually compatible activities have inhibition 0
work: Revelle & Condon 2015 draft, doi:10.1016/j.jrp.2014.12.006 (Fig. 2 caption)
note: Default in Revelle's code: off-diagonal 1, diagonal 0.05 (046 §3.3).

statement: Operator set proposed for the algebra: instigate(a,i,F); inhibit(a,i,I); consume(a,i) for the dominant activity only; select(a) = argmax over i of T_i - N_i; couple(a, i→j) as displacement or substitution. In CTA: excite (e), self-inhibit (diag i), cross-inhibit (off-diagonal i), stimulate (s)
work: Proposed in 046 from Atkinson & Birch 1970 (as implemented, not read) and Revelle 2008 draft (https://personality-project.org/revelle/publications/cta.pdf; no DOI)
note: The file's own translation, not a claim of any source. 046 found no positive coupling (one person's action raising another's tendency) in either theory.

statement: High fear-of-failure subjects took longer to go to an achievement task after an anxiety manipulation (apparent computer breakdown) than low fear-of-failure subjects; a single study, supporting latency as the effect of inhibition
work: Blankenship 1987, doi:10.1037/0022-3514.53.2.361 (not read); as reported in Blankenship, Tumlinson & Sims 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740, and Revelle & Condon 2015
note: Second-hand. The anxiety manipulation is the file's own term for the induced condition; it is deliberate and deceptive, so ethics is tagged manipulation.

statement: Both motive groups shifted toward harder tasks over trials, with high-achievement subjects faster; the dynamic theory predicts the shift, the static model predicts none
work: Kuhl & Blankenship 1979, doi:10.1037/0033-295x.86.2.141 (not read); via Slade & Rush 1991, doi:10.1037/0022-3514.60.1.165, and Blankenship et al. 1995
note: Houtmans (1989) and Slade & Rush (1991) replicate the phenomenon per Blankenship et al.; Slade & Rush's own results not read.

statement: Persistence at easy and hard tasks: simulations could not model all experimental results, but differential persistence of low-resultant-motivation subjects was supported, contrary to Atkinson 1957
work: Blankenship 1992, Motivation and Emotion 16, 35-63, doi:10.1007/BF00996486 (not read); via Blankenship et al. 1995, doi:10.3758/BF03204740
note: Second-hand. Contradicts the static model's persistence prediction; see contradiction 8.

statement: Four-person CTA talking-time shares (published Table 3): four introverts (cues 0.95, 1.00, 1.05, 1.10) 0.24 0.25 0.24 0.27; four extraverts (cues 3.95, 4.00, 4.05, 4.10) 0.25 0.24 0.25 0.26; two introverts and two extraverts (cues 0.95, 1.00, 4.05, 4.10) 0.11 0.13 0.37 0.38
work: Revelle & Condon 2015 draft, doi:10.1016/j.jrp.2014.12.006 (Table 3); Revelle 2008 draft (https://personality-project.org/revelle/publications/cta.pdf; no DOI)
